HUD harness, 5 runs per task, 100 tasks: (1) HUD + Claude Opus 5.5: 67.3 ± 4.7 (run-to-run ±1.9), full-credit runs 26.6%, tasks >=1/5 47, 5/5 9, median steps 160, container 80 min. Tasks: 100 expert-authored tasks (24 public, 76 held out). Configurations: seven models in one HUD harness with provider-native tools. Baseline: none designated (paired tests against top model). Held constant: task, prompt, container (~2 vCPUs, offline), resources, 1,000-step budget, grader; empty agent parameters, no system prompt; differs in tool interface and agent loop per provider and reasoning setting (platform default high effort). Acceptance tests: calibrated hidden graders (reference = 1.0, untouched and inert change = 0; control patches in nearly half the tasks). Repetitions: 5 runs per model and task (3,495 scored runs); step- or token-limit runs excluded and rerun. Human intervention: none

Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3) and GPT-6 Astra (63.7) lead and are not separable (Δ +3.6, paired CI [-1.4, +9.7], p = 0.20); both ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 (Opus +20.8 [16.9, 25.3]); Fable ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (+6.5 [1.6, 10.5]); Gemini ahead of Qwen (+6.5 [3.0, 11.0]); Qwen, DeepSeek and Grok indistinguishable. Four tiers; all others p < 0.001 vs Opus. GPT-6 Astra more consistent (within-task SD 7.3 vs 13.6) and uses ~1/5 of Opus' steps; step count weakly related to score (r -0.15 to +0.17). Blockers/gates cost Opus 3.7 points, ranking unchanged

Yes: seven models span 35 points in four statistically distinct tiers, versus 0.9 points among four of them on DeepSWE v1.1 (indicative, not controlled). Task-sampling intervals (±3.3-5.5) are 2-10x run-to-run intervals. Authors' stated limits: per-provider native tool interfaces confound tool design with model capability; no reasoning-effort sweep; 100 tasks, differences < ~5 points not to be over-interpreted; repositories public and likely in training data

Limitations: harness differs per provider (part of gaps may reflect tools); reasoning effort not swept; sample size of 100 tasks; contamination of repository code and eventual leakage of public tasks. Future work: audit graders with an independent judge and publish disagreement rates; rerun under a shared single-tool harness; sweep reasoning effort; grow corpus and retire public tasks; extend to other domains (management consulting)
